title: Forces and motion — finding the net force
summary: Read force arrows, combine forces with direction, and connect net force to acceleration.

sections.title: 1. Arrows show size and direction
sections.markdown: A force has both **size** and **direction**. Forces pointing the same way add; forces pointing in opposite directions subtract. If 8 N pushes right and 5 N pushes left, the net force is 3 N to the right.

visualization.title: Forces acting on a cart
visualization.aria_label: A cart has an eight-newton arrow to the right and a five-newton arrow to the left, producing a three-newton net force to the right.
visualization.text_fallback: 8 N right minus 5 N left gives a net force of 3 N right.

sections.title: 2. Net force changes motion
sections.markdown: Newton's second law is $F_{net}=ma$. A larger net force gives more acceleration; a larger mass gives less acceleration for the same force. For a 4 kg cart with a 20 N net force, $a=20/4=5 m/s^2$.

sections.title: 3. Choose a positive direction
sections.markdown: Choose one direction as positive before calculating. If right is positive, a 7 N force left is $-7$ N. The sign records direction; it does not mean the force has a negative size.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
checkpoint.instructions: Use right as positive. Enter numbers only; include a minus sign for a leftward result.

questions.prompt: A box has 6 N right and 6 N left. What is the net force in newtons?
A cart has 9 N right and 5 N left. What is the net force?
questions.feedback: Subtract the opposing force from the larger force.

questions.prompt: A 4 kg cart has a 20 N net force. What is its acceleration?
What net force accelerates a 3 kg object at 4 m/s²?
Right is positive. What signed net force results from 2 N right and 5 N left?
questions.feedback: The larger force points left, so the answer is negative.
